scope: Separate stopping tolerance, periodic treatment, symmetry restrictions, initial registry, and electronic model effects

sequence.question: Did the coarse force threshold stop relaxation prematurely?
sequence.setting: Same coarse endpoint, Gamma base cell, same actual eight operations, tighten electronic accuracy to 0.01 and raw Fmax to 0.005 eV/A
sequence.interpretation: Still no network at tighter convergence rejects the stopping-threshold-only explanation at this sampling and constraint; does not prove a global or unconstrained minimum

sequence.question: Are relevant forces stable to periodic supercell enlargement?
sequence.setting: Same frozen tight geometry; compare 2x2x1, 2x2x2 and a larger in-plane grid as required; preserve base-cell atomic period and fold replica forces
sequence.interpretation: Do not attribute all differences solely to k-points; tblite periodic electrostatics can depend on the supercell treatment
sequence.gate: Choose a common sampling only after residual force changes are comfortably below the geometry stopping threshold; no production accuracy claim from one doubling

sequence.question: Do the extra half-b translation or the declared space-group operations prevent escape?
sequence.common_setting: Same GFN2 method, numerically checked common sampling, fixed cell, raw Fmax 0.005 eV/A
sequence.perturbations: Predeclare seeds 20261030 and 20261031 and paired signs. Remove global translation; project the same small displacement into each allowed space, normalize to maximum 0.02 A. For four-operation arm explicitly retain a component that breaks the extra b/2 translation; for free arm include a component outside the four-operation space. Save applied coordinates and covalent checks.
sequence.implementation_requirement: Do not call unconstrained automatic FixSymmetry detection to stand in for the declared four operations. Record rotations, translations, atom mappings, projector rank and raw forces.
sequence.interpretation: Eight-to-four recovery isolates extra translation restrictions; recovery only on full release implicates broader symmetry restrictions. Identical outcomes are evidence for these probes only, not exhaustive stability. Releasing constraints without perturbation is insufficient.

sequence.question: Is the initial chain registry controlling the outcome?
sequence.selection: Predeclare uniform phase indices 0, 6, 12, 18 on the approved 24-point grid; fixed independent template 0, chain x 0.25, rotation 0 degrees. Apply existing chemistry/overlap checks only; record any invalid entries without replacing them based on H bonds.
sequence.setting: Common method, sampling, cell and chosen symmetry protocol
sequence.report: Retain each starting and ending identity, continuous N-O/H-O/angle values, network rank, energy, and raw force. Geometric existence of a network is not energetic stability.

sequence.question: Does GFN2 give a different force landscape from independent electronic methods?
sequence.setting: Cloud DFT on the same frozen control geometries and selected small collective displacements, with independently converged PBE-D3(BJ)+ATM; check key disagreements with r2SCAN-D4
sequence.report: N/O/NH force vectors, collective displacement gradients, local curvature or scan shape, and matched-setting relative energies
sequence.interpretation: Method error becomes a stronger explanation only after sampling and geometry freedom are matched. Molecular GFN2 benchmarks do not validate periodic PA6. A single DFT functional is not an unquestioned reference.

sequence.question: Does fixed-cell strain matter?
sequence.setting: Only after prior comparisons, relax selected a/b/c/gamma freedoms for a representative using otherwise matched conditions
sequence.interpretation: Keep cell effects separate from changed sampling, starting geometry, and symmetry. Near-zero mean pressure does not imply small anisotropic stress.
